newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish primary T-bill dealers down to 54 in Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Polish primary T-bill dealers down to 54 in Q1 '97.

text.p: The number of Polish primary T-bill dealers fell in the first quarter of 1997 to 54 from 59 in the fourth quarter of 1996, the National Bank of Poland said in a statement.
The status of a primary T-bill dealer entitles banks and non-banking institutions to buy Polish treasury bills directly at the finance ministry's regular primary tenders each Monday.
The group of banks with the privilege decreased by Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA in Lublin, Bank Staropolski SA in Poznan and Westdeutsche Landesbank Poland SA in Warsaw.
The total number of banks with a primary T-bill dealer status in the first quarter of 1997 fell to 45 against 48 in fourth quarter of 1996.

Out of the domestic non-banking sector, the Narodowy Fundusz Ochrony Srodowiska i Gospodarki Wodnej environment fund and Poland's largest insurer Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU) lost the privilege, cutting the total number of non-banking dealers to nine.

Those financial institutions which will buy 15.07 million zlotys, in nominal terms, worth of T-bills during the first quarter of 1997 will receive the privilege in the second quarter. The purchase requirement was 18.5 million zlotys in the last quarter of 1996.
